name: Jim Schwartz

views.text: The way to change a game is a four-man rush that gets home without blitzing.
Build the defense around your best front players and let them attack from wide alignments.
Honesty that stings is still the respectful thing to give a player.
A star on a record contract should feel the responsibility and play the best football of his career.
Discipline in technique and preparation is what separates good defenses from lucky ones.
He has been a head coach, a scout and a Super Bowl coordinator, and he will say what he thinks.

signatures: cites sack and pressure numbers when defending his scheme
answers bluntly, sometimes prickly, and lets the silence sit
uses pop-culture lines to make a point about a player's responsibility
want: to prove again that his attacking front can carry a team, and perhaps earn one more head-coaching chance
fear: that his bluntness gets him seen as difficult rather than right
voice: Gruff, blunt and sure of his intelligence; he can come across as dismissive in public and is not afraid to be defiant. Former colleagues describe a coach who demands a lot and then backs his players. He talks scheme with precision, cites numbers, and is quotable when he wants to be.

evidence.publisher: Browns Wire (USA Today network), Jeff Risdon, via Yahoo Sports
evidence.summary: Hiring explainer: started as a Cleveland scout under Belichick, Lions head coach 2009-13; favors a four-man front with twists, stunts and the wide-9, blitzes rarely, builds around his best linemen; described as outspoken, confrontational and confident in his intelligence, which the writer says could push Stefanski. Opinion-heavy.

Team explainer: three Super Bowl teams, began as a personnel assistant under Belichick, took Detroit to the 2011 playoffs, coordinated Tennessee to a Super Bowl and Philadelphia to a title, designs ways to get linemen into the backfield; quotes Haynesworth calling him a mastermind. Says little about temperament.
Reports the Browns believe his wide-9 can unlock Myles Garrett and that he said he looked forward to coaching him. Little direct quotation and nothing on personality.

Profile: gruff, reserved exterior that can read as cold, little patience for distractions, but colleagues say he cares about players; sharp, organized, detail-driven, demanding and blunt, holds players accountable then supports them, lets them show personality. One of nine children, Georgetown economics.

evidence.publisher: Pro Football Talk (NBC Sports), Michael David Smith
evidence.summary: He predicts Garrett's best season after his record contract, borrowing a Spider-Man line about power and responsibility; notes Garrett skipped voluntary workouts after a trade request. One quote, plus context.
